questions.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3},{X}_{4}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼Po(\theta )$ with unknown rate parameter $\theta .$ You're given the particular sample

$$
{x}_{1}=4,\,{x}_{2}=2,\,{x}_{3}=1,\,{x}_{4}=2.
$$

The log-likelihood function of the sample is given by

$$
l(\theta )=a\theta +b\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\operatorname{ln}⁡c.
$$

Find the value of $a+b+c.$

*Hint: The probability mass function for a Poisson distribution is given by* 

$$
f(x)=\frac{{\theta }^{x}{e}^{-\theta }}{x!},\,x=0,1,2,…
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed discrete random variables with probability mass function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the log-likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡L(\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i},\theta )) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(f({x}_{i},\theta )).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=4$ independent Poisson random variables with unknown parameter $\theta .$ Therefore, the probability mass function is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,\theta ) & ={e}^{-\theta }\cdot \frac{{\theta }^{x}}{x!}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the log-likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-\theta }\cdot \frac{{\theta }^{{x}_{i}}}{{x}_{i}!}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-\theta })+\operatorname{ln}⁡({\theta }^{{x}_{i}})-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{i}!) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(-\theta )+{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({\theta }^{{x}_{i}})-{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{i}!) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(-\theta )+{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\theta )-{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{i}!) \\  & =-\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}1+\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}-{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{i}!) \\  & =-n\theta +\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}-\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}!)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the sample data with $n=4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}! & =4!\cdot 2!\cdot 1!\cdot 2!=24\cdot 2\cdot 1\cdot 2=96, \\ {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} & =4+2+1+2=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, substituting the above values into our expression for $l(\theta ),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =-4\theta +9\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\operatorname{ln}⁡96.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
a+b+c=-4+9+96=101.
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼B(6,\theta )$ with unknown probability of success $\theta .$ You're given the particular sample 

$$
{x}_{1}=4,\,{x}_{2}=3,\,{x}_{3}=5.
$$

The log-likelihood function of the sample is given by

$$
l(\theta )=\operatorname{ln}⁡a+b\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +c\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ).
$$

Find the value of $a+b+c.$

*Hint: The probability mass function for a binomial random variable is given by*

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{x}){\theta }^{x}(1-\theta )^{6-x},\,x=0,1,…,6.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed discrete random variables with probability mass function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the log-likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡L(\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i},\theta )) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(f({x}_{i},\theta )).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=3$ independent binomial random variables with an unknown probability of success $\theta $ and $N=6$ as the number of trials. Therefore, the probability mass function is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,\theta ) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{N}{x}){\theta }^{x}(1-\theta )^{N-x},\,x=0,1,…,N \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{x}){\theta }^{x}(1-\theta )^{6-x},\,x=0,1,…,6.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the log-likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡((\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{{x}_{i}}){\theta }^{{x}_{i}}(1-\theta )^{6-{x}_{i}}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{{x}_{i}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡({\theta }^{{x}_{i}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡((1-\theta )^{6-{x}_{i}}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{{x}_{i}})+{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(6-{x}_{i})\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{{x}_{i}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ){\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(6-{x}_{i}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{{x}_{i}})+S\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(6n-S)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta )\end{aligned}
$$

where $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}.$

Now, note that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{{x}_{i}}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{{x}_{1}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{{x}_{2}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{{x}_{3}}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{{x}_{i}})).\end{aligned}
$$

So, our expression for $l(\theta )$ becomes

$$
l(\theta )=\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{{x}_{i}}))+S\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(6n-S)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ).
$$

Now, using the sample data with $n=3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{{x}_{i}}) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{4})\cdot (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{3})\cdot (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{5}) \\  & =15\cdot 20\cdot 6 \\  & =1\,800,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
S=4+3+5=12.
$$

Substituting the above values into our expression for $l(\theta )$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1\,800)+12\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(6\cdot 3-12)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡1\,800+12\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +6\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
a+b+c=1\,800+12+6=1\,818.
$$

Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{5}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼B(3,\theta )$ with unknown probability of success $\theta .$ You're given the particular sample 

$$
{x}_{1}=2,\,{x}_{2}=1,\,{x}_{3}=3,\,{x}_{4}=1,\,{x}_{5}=1.
$$

The log-likelihood function of the sample is given by

$$
l(\theta )=\operatorname{ln}⁡a+b\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +c\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ).
$$

Find the value of $a+b+c.$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed discrete random variables with probability mass function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the log-likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡L(\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i},\theta )) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(f({x}_{i},\theta )).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=5$ independent binomial random variables with an unknown probability of success $\theta $ and $N=3$ as the number of trials. Therefore, the probability mass function is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,\theta ) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{N}{x}){\theta }^{x}(1-\theta )^{N-x},\,x=0,1,…,N \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{x}){\theta }^{x}(1-\theta )^{3-x},\,x=0,1,2,3.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the log-likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡((\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{{x}_{i}}){\theta }^{{x}_{i}}(1-\theta )^{3-{x}_{i}}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{{x}_{i}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡({\theta }^{{x}_{i}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡((1-\theta )^{3-{x}_{i}}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{{x}_{i}})+{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(3-{x}_{i})\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{{x}_{i}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ){\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(3-{x}_{i}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{{x}_{i}})+S\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(3n-S)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta )\end{aligned}
$$

where $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}.$

Now, note that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{{x}_{i}}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{{x}_{1}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{{x}_{2}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{{x}_{3}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{{x}_{4}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{{x}_{5}}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{{x}_{i}})).\end{aligned}
$$

So, our expression for $l(\theta )$ becomes

$$
l(\theta )=\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{{x}_{i}}))+S\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(3n-S)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ).
$$

Now, using the sample data with $n=5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{{x}_{i}}) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{2})\cdot (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1})\cdot (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{3})\cdot (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1})\cdot (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1}) \\  & =3\cdot 3\cdot 1\cdot 3\cdot 3 \\  & =81,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
S=2+1+3+1+1=8.
$$

Substituting the above values into our expression for $l(\theta )$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(81)+8\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(3\cdot 5-8)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(81)+8\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +7\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
a+b+c=81+8+7=96.
$$
